Not every engine incident demands a total unit replacement. Where failure is isolated (e.g. snapped at cranking speed), targeted repair may be viable. EnginesMarket enables you to compare both repair and replacement options side by side.

ordered.title: Interference vs. Non-Interference: What Happens When It Snaps?
ordered.description: This fundamental design difference dictates whether a snapped timing belt writes off your engine or simply requires a £350 roadside belt replacement.

cards.title: Examples:
cards.text: ⚠ Interference Engine Valves open into the piston travel zone. When the belt snaps, pistons smash into open valves, destroying head, valves, and pistons. £2,500 – £7,000+ (Replacement Engine) Examples: Over 95% of modern cars: Ford EcoBoost, VW/Audi TSI/TDI, BMW petrols, Mercedes, Honda VTEC, Toyota VVT-i, PSA PureTech / BlueHDi.
cards.fullText: ⚠ Interference Engine Valves open into the piston travel zone. When the belt snaps, pistons smash into open valves, destroying head, valves, and pistons. £2,500 – £7,000+ (Replacement Engine) Examples: Over 95% of modern cars: Ford EcoBoost, VW/Audi TSI/TDI, BMW petrols, Mercedes, Honda VTEC, Toyota VVT-i, PSA PureTech / BlueHDi.

cards.title: Examples:
cards.text: ✓ Non-Interference Engine Clearance exists between fully open valves and top dead centre piston crowns. When belt snaps, engine stops with zero internal contact. £300 – £800 (Fit New Belt & Retime) Examples: Older engines: select Ford Zetec 1.25/1.6/2.0, pre-2000 Honda B-series, early Toyota 1.8 7A-FE / Mazda Miata engines.
cards.fullText: ✓ Non-Interference Engine Clearance exists between fully open valves and top dead centre piston crowns. ordered.title: Common Questions About Timing Belt Failure Answered

blocks.question: How much does timing belt replacement cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Typical timing belt replacement costs range from £300 to £800 for a 4-cylinder engine. A belt + water pump package adds £100–£300. Labour ranges from 3–6 hours at £65–£95/hr at an independent specialist. → View full Timing Belt Replacement Cost Guide

blocks.question: What happens if a timing belt breaks while driving? +
blocks.answer: On an interference engine (the vast majority of vehicles built after 2000), the camshaft stops turning while the crankshaft continues spinning. Pistons smash into open valves, bending valve stems, cracking pistons, and damaging cylinder heads. Total engine repair or replacement costs £2,500–£7,000+.

blocks.question: Can I drive with a worn timing belt? +
blocks.answer: No. A timing belt gives almost no warning before failure. If you are overdue by mileage or years (rubber naturally degrades over time), replace it immediately without waiting for audible symptoms.

blocks.question: How often should a timing belt be replaced? +
blocks.answer: Most manufacturers specify replacement every 60,000–100,000 miles or every 5–8 years, whichever comes first. Always check your vehicle handbook as rubber deteriorates with time regardless of mileage.

blocks.question: My car has a timing chain — do I need a belt replacement? +
blocks.answer: No. Timing chain engines do not have scheduled replacement intervals, though some specific engines (such as BMW N47 or Land Rover Ingenium) may suffer early tensioner or guide failure. Chains typically provide an audible warning rattle on cold startup before failing. → View Timing Chain Failure Guide

blocks.question: Is a timing belt covered under warranty? +
blocks.answer: On used cars, timing belts are classed as consumable service items and are excluded from standard warranties. On reconditioned replacement engines, a brand-new timing belt is installed as part of the rebuild process.
